name: boostbox-client
summary: Store a boost's Podcasting 2.0 metadata in a BoostBox instance and get back a short URL for the payment description, with the API key held server-side.

source.note: Written for this catalog against the documented HTTP API of BoostBox (https://github.com/noblepayne/boostbox, MIT). No BoostBox source is redistributed here. The pattern it replaces is live: a Podcasting 2.0 site reads NEXT_PUBLIC_BOOSTBOX_API_KEY from client components, which serves the key to every visitor.

peer.next: >=14 (App Router) - route.ts is a Next.js route handler

env.name: BOOSTBOX_API_KEY
env.why: Sent as the X-Api-Key header. Must NOT carry a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix: Next.js inlines every NEXT_PUBLIC_* value into the browser bundle at build time, so a prefixed key is served to everyone who loads the page. Adding the prefix to silence an import error puts the key back in the bundle.

env.name: BOOSTBOX_URL
env.why: Base URL of your BoostBox instance. The route builds its target from this and never from the request, so the route cannot be used as a proxy to somewhere else.

caveats: This code has never served production traffic. It is written against BoostBox's documented API, not extracted from a site that runs it.

The route refuses to start if BOOSTBOX_API_KEY is still 'v4v4me'. That is the default shipped with BoostBox itself, so anyone who knows the project knows it, and a deployment still using it is an open write endpoint.
Only the fields BoostBox documents are forwarded. A route that relays whatever it was handed is a way to send arbitrary bodies to another service using your credentials.
String fields are truncated to 4096 characters so one caller cannot walk your instance into its 413.
Nothing here proves a payment happened. BoostBox stores what you tell it; a boost record is a claim, not a receipt.
Submit before you pay. receipt.desc is the payment description you want to send, so the metadata stays reachable through a wallet that drops custom TLV records.
GET /boost/{id} is not wrapped. It needs no key and returns an HTML page with the JSON in a URL-encoded x-rss-payment header; call it directly if you need it.
